question:
DRAG DROP -
A network administrator must automate the process of pinging all the IP addresses from the 10.0.0.0/8 subnet. The subnet is already present on the ARP table of the Cisco Nexus switch. Drag and drop the bash commands to generate the desired output. Not all commands are used.

Expected output:
--- 10.1.0.2 ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 5 packets received, 0.00% packet loss
--- 10.1.0.77 ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100.00% packet loss
theory: This pipeline chains NX-OS CLI access from Bash ('vsh -c') with standard Linux text tools: filtering the ARP table output down to IPv4 address lines, transforming each surviving line into a 'ping <address>' command, and then narrowing the resulting ping output to just the summary statistics/loss lines — the same style of Guest/Bash-shell scripting the book uses to fan an NX-OS CLI command out into repeatable per-address automation without writing a full Python script. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
